prompt: Stage 2-4 carousel, 88 HP, level 5. You hold one AD component. Your board is a mixed opener with no vertical. The carousel offers a Spatula, a completed defensive item on a 2-cost tank, and an AD component. What do you take?

options.label: The Spatula: emblems win games and you can decide the trait later
The completed defensive item on the 2-cost tank: an item now plus a unit you can play
The AD component to pair with the one you hold

explanation:
A Spatula is only an item once you have a trait worth an emblem, and at 2-4 with a mixed board you do not. It sits on the bench as a dead component through stage 3, the stage where losses start to cost real HP, and there is a fair chance it never becomes anything better than the trait you happened to fall into. The completed tank item is two components of value on a unit you can put on the board immediately, and it stabilises the frontline for the stage 3 rounds you are about to play at 1-loss. That is the most item power you can use this round.

The AD component is the tempting one because it completes a pair: but a pair of AD components makes one carry item on a 1-star 2-cost, while the carousel is offering a finished item for free. Take the finished item, keep your AD component for the 3-4 carousel or a shop drop, and make the emblem decision when there is a trait to make it about.
principle: A Spatula without a plan is a dead component; a completed item without a plan is still an item.
commonMistake: Taking the Spatula reflexively because emblems are strong, then carrying it uncombined into stage 4.
